targets.authors: Wiese, I.S., Ré, R., Steinmacher, I., Kuroda, R.T, Oliva, G.A., Treude C., Gerosa, M.A.
targets.title: Using contextual information to predict co-changes.
targets.evidence_quote:
Our research is defined as an external and conceptual
replication of the baseline study published in [3].
targets.outcome_quote:
Overall we could say we were able to confirm the
findings in [3]. On the other hand, we observe that these
rates are biased towards the granularity, i.e., commit
level or file-pair level. This difference points out that it
is more challenging to predict all entities that will be cochanged in a single commit than to predict whether a
particular entity will be co-changed with the target file
in a single commit. According to our point of view, it is
more useful to succeed the former than the latter.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly confirm the original aggregate performance, but their central message is that this evaluation does not represent the practical claim of recommending all files to change in a commit. They show substantially worse performance with the practically appropriate evaluation. This is the main methodological critique, not a minor limitation; the explicit overall confirmation takes priority over individual project comparisons.

reasoning: The authors independently mine development histories through 2018, construct new training/test samples and retest Wiese et al.’s predictive finding. The shared software projects do not make this an analysis of the original supplied dataset. Only Wiese et al. is a target; other cited co-change studies are background.
